message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need to know | |---------|-----------------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when you finish a round. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (1–9, two of each; 2× “Skip”, “Reverse”, “Draw Two”; 4× “Wild”, 4× “Wild Draw Four”). | | **Setup** | 1. Shuffle the deck.
2. Deal 7 cards to each player.
3. Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
4. Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two,” the first player draws two and loses a turn). | | **Turn Play** | On your turn you may:
• **Play** one card that matches either the color or the value of the top discard card.
• **Play** a Wild or Wild Draw Four (any color).
• **Draw** one card from the draw pile if you cannot play. If that card can be played, you may do so immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction (two players: acts like Skip).
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk being challenged.) | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player starts their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards all their cards, the round ends. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbered cards = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Winning the Game** | First to reach 500 points (or your chosen target) wins. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep an eye on the discard pile** – you can often anticipate what the next player will need to play. 2. **Use Wild Draw Four wisely** – it’s powerful but risky if you’re caught playing it illegally. 3. **Plan your “UNO” call** – remember to say it before the next player takes a turn, not after. 4. **Stacking** – some house rules allow stacking Draw Twos or Draw Fours; clarify before starting. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
